RoomType.rationale: CubexConstructNormal.RoomType => RoomType.Monster (CubexConstructNormal.cs:9). Sim carries no room_type field on the Encounter dataclass; 'cubex_construct' is placed in rooms.py:101's normal_keys for _overgrowth_rooms() (seam/rooms_and_map owns the picker itself). GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) matches EncounterModel.cs:70/89's Monster=>10/20 defaults, which CubexConstructNormal does not override.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: No sim counterpart. C#'s only consumers of AllPossibleMonsters are ActModel.AllMonsters (ActModel.cs:169, read only by ModelDb.Monsters -> UnlockConsoleCmd.cs:68/147's dev-console 'monsters' listing and NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164's stats-screen ratio label) and the Bestiary screen (NBestiary.cs:194) -- all UI/dev-console, zero gameplay or RNG effect, confirmed by reading every caller in src/. The headless sim has neither surface, so omitting a counterpart costs nothing observable.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: CubexConstructNormal.GenerateMonsters (CubexConstructNormal.cs:13-16) returns a single-element list: (ModelDb.Monster<CubexConstruct>().ToMutable(), null) -- zero base.Rng calls, one monster, no slot. Sim's monster_classes=[CubexConstruct], no slots/monster_slots set (defaults (), sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) and create_monsters draws no RNG for composition (the default implementation this encounter inherits, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py). Roster (1x CubexConstruct), order (trivial), slot (null/none on both sides) and draw count (0 == 0) all match.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: (structural -- Encounter dataclass has no hook methods)
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by CubexConstructNormal. The sim's Encounter dataclass (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) declares no hook methods and is never passed to HookSystem.register -- it is plain data, structurally incapable of joining the hook walk, which reproduces 'the encounter itself is not a listener' exactly.

guards.what: MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward gold ladder (the encounter brief's 5th thing to verdict)
guards.rationale: CubexConstructNormal does not override MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward, so both inherit EncounterModel.cs:64-100's RoomType ladder (Monster=10-20) times AscensionHelper.PovertyAscensionGoldMultiplier under AscensionLevel.Poverty. CUBEX_CONSTRUCT_NORMAL carries min_gold=None, max_gold=None (Encounter dataclass default, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py), so rewards.py:886-887 falls back to GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) -- the same ladder. Ascension (Poverty) scaling is out of scope by the audit contract (rewards.py:32's explicit 'no Scarcity/Poverty scaling').

guards.what: EncounterModel.Rng independence (per the encounter brief: verify the sim does not draw encounter rolls off a shared/run-level stream)
guards.rationale: CubexConstructNormal.GenerateMonsters makes zero base.Rng calls (CubexConstructNormal.cs:13-16, confirmed by reading the whole method) and the sim's create_monsters counterpart makes zero calls to any Rng/random.Random for composition -- there is nothing here for stream identity to diverge on. (Draw-count fact only; which named stream backs EncounterModel.Rng in general is seam/rng_streams' mechanism, already verdicted faithful for the seeding formula at rng_streams step 21.)
